checks.name: go
checks.run: go test -timeout 30m ./... && go vet ./... && test -z "$(gofmt -l .)" && go mod tidy -diff && GOOS=linux go build ./... && GOOS=windows go build ./...

tasks.title: Move the two brief skills into the plugin as create-brief and review-brief, with their budgets
tasks.goal: Every repository that loads the vloop plugin should be able to write a brief with /vloop:create-brief and have it reviewed with /vloop:review-brief; today the two skills live only in this repository's .claude/skills/, labelled experimental. This task copies them into plugin/skills/ under their plugin names, drops the experimental label, points them at each other and at /vloop:operate, fixes create-brief's structure-check step, changes /vloop:operate's description to name /vloop:create-brief, and gives the two skills word ceilings of their own. The move is a move: the skills' instructions stay as they are beyond these changes, and the project copies under .claude/skills/ stay where they are (removing them is the operator's, at close).

references.why: the skill that moves to plugin/skills/create-brief/, with guidelines.md and templates/ beside it copied byte for byte; its text changes only in K1's renames, pointers and step 5.1
the skill that moves to plugin/skills/review-brief/; its text changes only in the name, the description's prefix and the pointer to /vloop:create-brief and ../create-brief/guidelines.md
Skills gains create-brief and review-brief after verify; Ceilings gains 1200 and 1000 with the brief's dated comment (L10) — never a number taken from the skills' size after the run
the plugin's structural checks (TestPluginSkills) the two new skills must pass as they are, without weakening any check
only its frontmatter description's last sentence changes; its body (1749 words, one under its ceiling) must not move by a word
TestWorkedExampleB7PluginPath pins the extracted skill list, which this task changes to the eight names and nothing else

acceptance: plugin/skills/ holds exactly eight skill folders: create-brief, gate-review, operate, plan, review, review-brief, verify, work. plugin/skills/create-brief/ holds exactly SKILL.md, guidelines.md and templates/ (with brief-en.md and brief-es.md); plugin/skills/review-brief/ holds exactly SKILL.md.

plugin/skills/create-brief/guidelines.md, templates/brief-en.md and templates/brief-es.md are byte for byte the files under .claude/skills/vloop-create-brief/; the .claude/skills/ project copies are left in place, unchanged.

Line 2 of the two SKILL.md files is `name: create-brief` and `name: review-brief`; each `description` is the original one with its leading "Experimental, not yet in the plugin — " dropped and the rest kept. No file under plugin/skills/ contains vloop-create-brief, vloop-review-brief, "experimental" or "not yet in the plugin" (case-insensitive).

create-brief's SKILL.md names /vloop:review-brief for the independent review (its step 5) and /vloop:operate for marking ready and running (its step 6). review-brief's SKILL.md names /vloop:create-brief as the skill briefs are written with, and its standard as the guidelines.md beside /vloop:create-brief's SKILL.md (../create-brief/guidelines.md from its folder).

create-brief's step 5.1 says to copy the brief, under the same file name, into a temporary directory outside docs/briefs/, because vloop brief check compares the file name with the brief's name. A violation the review must rule on: any other change to either skill's instructions beyond the name, the description's prefix, the skill pointers and this step — the move is a move.

plugin/skills/operate/SKILL.md's frontmatter description ends `Writing briefs is /vloop:create-brief's.` in place of `Writing briefs is not this skill's job.`; nothing else in that file changes, and no other existing skill's file changes.

internal/budget/budget.go: Skills is plan, gate-review, work, review, operate, verify, create-brief, review-brief, in that order; Ceilings gains "create-brief": 1200 and "review-brief": 1000, each with the comment `// 2026-11-02, B28 (#101): its size when it joined the plugin, plus headroom`; the other ceilings are unchanged. budget.Check on a plugin whose create-brief SKILL.md is padded to 1201 words reports `create-brief: 1,201 words, over its ceiling of 1,200`.

With a binary built from the tree: `vloop fence check --phase review --root . --tool skill --path review-brief` prints allow and exits 0; with `--path vloop-review-brief` it prints `deny: skill vloop-review-brief is not vloop's — use /vloop:review` and exits 1; `vloop plugin path` in a freshly initialised repository extracts a plugin whose skills/create-brief/templates holds brief-en.md and brief-es.md. These follow from the embedded plugin's skill list: no change to internal/fence, internal/driver, the fences or vloop brief new/check.

vloop doctor in a repository with agent.review = copilot, a stub copilot and a .claude/skills/review-brief/ folder exits 1 and prints `✗ .claude/skills/review-brief has the name of vloop's review-brief skill; a copilot session may load it instead — rename it`.

Committed tests, run by the `go` check, cover the new behaviour: a budget test that pads create-brief past 1,200 words and expects the message above, and a doctor test in internal/cli (as internal/cli/doctor_copilot_plan_test.go) for the review-brief clash line. A task that leaves neither behind is a violation. TestPluginSkills passes on the plugin with the two new skills, no structural check weakened.

TestWorkedExampleB7PluginPath in cmd/vloop/b7_e2e_test.go is changed to the eight skill names and nothing else; the work notes name the contract item (K1, the eight folders) and that this is the only earlier test changed.

tasks.title: Add the Go test that holds each plugin brief template to the binary's
tasks.goal: The plugin's brief templates are a copy of the binary's templates (internal/brief/templates/<language>.md) with an executive-summary section added, and nothing generates them, so they can drift. This task adds a Go test that fails when a plugin template, with its executive-summary section removed, differs from the binary's template of the same language, or has no executive-summary heading at all. It reads the repository's own plugin and templates by relative path, as TestPluginSkills reads ../../plugin, and proves its failures with fixtures on copies in temporary directories. Neither the templates nor the binary's templates are edited to make it pass.

references.why: the binary's English template the plugin's brief-en.md must equal outside its `## Executive summary` section; it is not edited
the binary's Spanish template the plugin's brief-es.md must equal outside its `## Resumen ejecutivo` section; it is not edited
the pattern the new test follows: a check that is a function of directories, run on the repository's own (../../plugin) and on fixture copies

acceptance: A committed Go test — a new top-level test function, in any package and under any name, not a case added inside a test that exists at the base — compares each of plugin/skills/create-brief/templates/brief-en.md and brief-es.md, minus the lines from its executive-summary heading (`## Executive summary`, `## Resumen ejecutivo`) up to but not including the next line starting `## `, with internal/brief/templates/en.md and es.md byte for byte, and passes on the repository as it is.

The comparison is a function of the plugin directory and the binary's template directory; the test runs it on the repository's own (by relative path, as TestPluginSkills reads ../../plugin) and committed fixture tests run it on copies in temporary directories, covering each planted failure below. A test that only reads the repository's files and has no fixture proving it fails is a violation.

A heading of brief-en.md changed outside the executive summary makes the test fail with `plugin/skills/create-brief/templates/brief-en.md differs from internal/brief/templates/en.md outside its executive summary`; a change to internal/brief/templates/es.md makes it fail with the brief-es.md / es.md form of that message.

brief-es.md without its `## Resumen ejecutivo` heading makes the test fail with `plugin/skills/create-brief/templates/brief-es.md has no executive summary` (and likewise for brief-en.md without `## Executive summary`).
A line changed or added inside a template's executive summary is not a difference: the test passes. The messages name both files as paths under the repository root, with forward slashes on every OS.
No template, plugin or binary, is edited, and vloop brief new/check are unchanged.

tasks.title: Name /vloop:create-brief and /vloop:review-brief in the CLAUDE.md section vloop writes
tasks.goal: The CLAUDE.md section that vloop init writes and vloop upgrade refreshes is how an interactive session in any repository learns which vloop skill to follow. This task changes its interactive-session paragraph so it also sends a session to /vloop:create-brief to write a brief and to /vloop:review-brief to review one in a separate session. Every other line of the section stays as it is; upgrade replaces an older section between the markers with no change to its logic.

references.why: install.Section, whose interactive-session paragraph becomes the brief's K3 line, verbatim and as one line; every other line, the markers and MergeClaudeMD stay as they are

acceptance: install.Section's interactive-session paragraph is, as one line and verbatim: `In an interactive session you are the operator's hands: follow the operator's playbook (/vloop:operate), not these session rules. To write a brief, follow /vloop:create-brief; to review one, run /vloop:review-brief in a separate session. If /vloop:operate is not available, the vloop plugin is not loaded: say so, give the user the two ways to load it (claude plugin install vloop@vloop after claude plugin marketplace add mvelosop/vloop, or claude --plugin-dir "$(vloop plugin path)"), and meanwhile work from vloop --help.` Every other line of the section is unchanged.

`vloop init` in a fresh git repository writes a CLAUDE.md that is the section, in which `grep -c '/vloop:create-brief' CLAUDE.md` prints 1; install.MergeClaudeMD on a CLAUDE.md holding an older section between the markers replaces it with the new one and keeps everything outside the markers byte for byte.

The existing tests that pin the section's text (internal/install/install_test.go) change only to the new paragraph, and the work notes name the contract item (K3); a committed test asserts the new paragraph, run by the `go` check. A section change with no test pinning the new line is a violation.
This repository's own CLAUDE.md is not edited (the operator's, at close), and vloop init's output gains no hint.

tasks.title: Add an eval case for each brief skill and update the evals README and guide
tasks.goal: Each plugin skill's behaviour is checked by eval cases that the operator runs with claude plugin eval; the two new skills need one each. This task adds review-brief-planted-faults, a draft brief with three planted faults that /vloop:review-brief must name without editing the brief, and create-brief-drafts-checked, a settled request that /vloop:create-brief must turn into a checked draft, graded from the trace because the brief's file name is only known at run time. It also lists both in plugin/evals/README.md and fixes the evals guide's stale case count and suites table. No gate or task runs an eval: the run is the operator's, at close.

references.why: the cases' structure (case.yaml, prompt.md, scaffold.sh, graders/) the two new cases follow, and the table of other cases that gains a row for each
the case format, the grader types, and the operator's --allow-tools list every Bash grant a case names must be in (TestEvalGrantsCoverFence); its suite size and suites table change
the structural eval checks and TestEvalGrantsCoverFence the two cases must pass as they are, without weakening any check

acceptance: plugin/evals/review-brief-planted-faults/ invokes /vloop:review-brief on a scaffolded repository holding a draft brief that plants three faults: a fact about the code that the scaffolded code contradicts, a literal value the Behaviour contract and the Worked example state differently, and a configured check that fails after the first task and stays red until the last. Its graders, of any documented type: one that the verdict is not PASS; one per planted fault that it is named (three); one that the brief is not edited. Graders that could all pass with a planted fault missed, or with the brief edited, are a violation.

plugin/evals/create-brief-drafts-checked/ invokes /vloop:create-brief on a scaffolded repository with a request that settles every fork, states every literal value, and says the independent review is out of the case. Its graders read the trace, not a file: a tool_used Bash grader for `vloop brief new` and one for `vloop brief check`, each min 1; a regex grader on the trace for the check's `0 warning(s)` (vloop brief check prints it on its own line, `  ok, 0 warning(s)`, after the per-check lines); an llm grader with `focus: trace` that the brief written has `status: draft`, an executive summary, and the request's literal values verbatim. Graders that could pass with no brief written are a violation.

Both cases follow plugin/evals/README.md and docs/guide/evals.md: case.yaml declaring the scaffold, prompt.md with max_turns and allowed_tools holding at least the work fence's grants, graders of the documented types; every Bash grant either case names is in the guide's --allow-tools list. TestPluginSkills and TestEvalGrantsCoverFence pass in the `go` check with the two cases, no check weakened.

plugin/evals/README.md's table of other cases gains a row for each: `| `review-brief-planted-faults` | `/vloop:review-brief` | … |` and `| `create-brief-drafts-checked` | `/vloop:create-brief` | … |`.

docs/guide/evals.md says the full suite is `21 cases × 3 runs × 2 arms`; its "vloop's suites" table gains a row each for /vloop:create-brief (create-brief-drafts-checked), /vloop:review-brief (review-brief-planted-faults), /vloop:verify (verify-planted-mismatches) and /vloop:operate (operate-proposes-options); the line "`/vloop:operate` has no suite: it is the operator's, interactive." is removed. No other existing case changes.

tasks.title: Close the run: every gate at once and the worked example line for line
tasks.goal: The earlier tasks each prove one item; this one proves they hold together on the finished tree. It runs every gate of the run at once and walks the brief's worked example line for line, fixing whatever no longer agrees — a stale count, a pointer, a test left on the old list — without widening any task's scope. If nothing needs fixing, the task is done with no change and says so.
acceptance: The gates of T1 to T5 pass together on the finished tree, and the `go` check passes in full.

Every line of the brief's worked example holds on the built tree, including each planted failure (the template test's two messages, the padded create-brief's budget message, doctor's review-brief clash line), each proven by a committed test.

Any fix this task makes is confined to what an earlier task's acceptance already required; it changes no other skill's instructions, no fence, the driver, or vloop brief new/check, and its notes list each fix and the contract item it serves.
